tasks.title: Consecutive-revert guard plus blocked-aware run summary
tasks.description:
Third and last layer of the stuck-task fix. It must work even if layers 1 and 2 (tasks 69 and 70) both miss, so do not assume either is in place.

Today `src/commands/run.ts:602` calls `await deps.validateTaskTests({ task, tasksFilePath, projectRoot })` and DISCARDS the return value. When validation returns { status: 'failed' } the task is reverted to in-progress, and selectNextTask (`src/task-selector.ts:48`) returns any in-progress task ahead of all pending work — so the loop re-picks that same task every iteration, forever. Last round this livelocked for three iterations on a task that was already finished.

Add an IN-MEMORY, per-run, per-task counter of consecutive validation reverts. At 2, set the task's status to 'blocked' with an explanatory note (say why: repeated post-iteration validation failure, and which command failed) and let the loop continue to other work. Reset a task's counter when it validates clean.

'blocked' is already fully plumbed — src/tasks-schema.json, the src/types.ts:23 status union and its validation, `cairn task set-status`, the `cairn status` display, and selectNextTask (which already skips blocked tasks). The only new code is the counter plus the summary change.

Do NOT persist the counter as a Task field — that would require types.ts, tasks-schema.json, and generate-tasks.md changes for no benefit; livelocks only matter within a single run, and an in-memory counter resets naturally on restart. The threshold is fixed at 2 — do NOT add a cairn.json knob.

THE COMPLETION FLAG NEEDS ATTENTION or this trades a visible livelock for a silent drop. `src/commands/run.ts:131` tells agents to create the completion flag when tasks.json has 'no remaining pending/in-progress tasks'. A blocked task is NEITHER, so the flag fires, completedByFlag goes true, and the final summary (~:654-673) prints 'ALL TASKS COMPLETE' with a blocked task sitting right there. Make the summary count and report blocked tasks distinctly, including inside the completedByFlag branch, and make the ntfy title/tags reflect it ('tada' is wrong when tasks are blocked).

TDD against test/commands/run.test.ts using the existing makeRunDeps/makeRunOpts harness: assert that one revert does NOT block, that two consecutive reverts set 'blocked' and the loop moves on to other work, that a clean validation resets the counter, and that the summary distinguishes blocked from all-complete. Write the tests first and watch them fail.

Do NOT modify `cairn.json`'s `healthCheck` value and do NOT run `./install.sh` — both are user-managed for this round (the binary is pinned to a frozen copy outside the repo and the health check is redirected to a throwaway outfile). Note the running loop uses the FROZEN binary, so changes you make to the loop's own source do not take effect until the user unpins and rebuilds after the round.
tasks.notes:
# Task #71 — Consecutive-revert guard plus blocked-aware run summary

## What changed (both in `src/commands/run.ts`; tests in `test/commands/run.test.ts`)

### 1. The guard (new step `k2`, right after `validateTaskTests`)

`validateTaskTests`'s return value is no longer discarded. Two new run-scoped locals
alongside `completedByFlag`/`corruptionEvents`:

- `consecutiveReverts: Map<number, number>` — taskId → consecutive `status: 'failed'`
  validations. **In-memory, per-run, not a Task field** (per the task spec — no
  `types.ts` / `tasks-schema.json` / `generate-tasks.md` churn; it resets naturally on
  restart, which is correct because a livelock only exists inside one run).
- `blockedByGuard: Set<number>` — only used as the summary's fallback count if the final
  tasks.json read throws.

Logic:
- `status === 'failed'` → increment. At `REVERT_BLOCK_THRESHOLD` (module const, **fixed
  at 2**, deliberately not a `cairn.json` knob) call `deps.blockTask(...)`, log to stdout
  AND to the iteration log, then **delete the counter entry**. Deleting matters: if a
  human unblocks the task mid-run it gets a fresh pair of attempts instead of re-blocking
  on the very first revert.
- `status === 'passed'` → delete the counter entry (clean validation resets).
- `'skipped'` / `'error'` → left untouched on purpose. `'error'` is `isCantRunError` /
  timeout — infrastructure, not evidence the task is stuck (that's task #69's layer), and
  it does **not** revert the task, so it can't livelock. Neither incrementing nor
  resetting is right for it, so it's a no-op.

The `blockTask` call is wrapped in try/catch — a failed write logs and the loop continues
rather than aborting the run.

Note text: `Blocked by cairn after N consecutive post-iteration test validation failures.
Last failing command — <summarizeFailure(validation.message)>`. `validation.message` for
a failure is already `` `${cmd}: ${output.trim().slice(-200)}` `` from
`test-validator.ts`, so the failing command is the prefix. New private helper
`summarizeFailure()` collapses whitespace to one line and caps at 300 chars so the note
stays readable in `cairn status`.

### 2. New dep `blockTask` on `RunRunDeps` (+ exported `BlockTaskOpts`)

`{ tasksFilePath, dataDir, taskId, note }`. Default impl routes through
`mutateTasksFile` from `tasks-file.ts` — the same locked / atomic / snapshotted path
every `cairn task` mutation takes, so this does NOT violate the "no direct writes to
tasks.json" rule. It sets `status = 'blocked'` and appends the note with the standard
` | ` separator. `'blocked'` needed no new plumbing: schema, `types.ts` union,
`set-status`, `cairn status` and `selectNextTask` (which skips it) all already handle it.

### 3. Blocked-aware final summary

`blockedCount` is computed in the `finally` from a fresh `deps.readTasksFile` of
tasks.json, **not** from `blockedByGuard`. That is deliberate — it also catches tasks an
*agent* blocked, and blocked tasks pre-dating this run. Wrapped in try/catch, falling
back to `blockedByGuard.size`. This read intentionally does NOT increment
`corruptionEvents` (the summary line has already been composed by then).

`allClear = completedByFlag && blockedCount === 0` is the new gate everywhere:

- `Tasks blocked: N` line printed whenever `N > 0` (both the flag path and the
  `selectNextTask → null` path).
- `Status: ALL TASKS COMPLETE` only when `allClear`; otherwise, if the flag fired,
  `Status: NO ACTIONABLE TASKS REMAIN — N blocked task(s) need attention`.
- ntfy: `tags` is `tada` only when `allClear`, else `warning`. Title is
  `Cairn - Complete` / `Cairn - Blocked` (new) / `Cairn - Stopped`.
- The narrated/ntfy body has four branches now (all-clear, flag+blocked, no-flag+blocked,
  no-flag).

**Why this mattered:** the agent prompt (`run.ts:131`) tells agents to create the
completion flag when there are "no remaining pending/in-progress tasks". A blocked task
is neither, so the flag fires and the old summary printed ALL TASKS COMPLETE with a
blocked task sitting right there — trading a visible livelock for a silent drop. The
prompt wording itself was left alone: with a blocked task there genuinely is no
actionable work, so the flag firing is correct; the summary is what had to change.

## Tests — 8 new in `test/commands/run.test.ts` (TDD, 5 red first)

`makeRunDeps` gained a `blockTask` mock. Two new local helpers inside `describe('runRun')`:

- `makeGuardDeps(tasks, overrides)` — wires deps to a **mutable task array**:
  `selectNextTask` behaves like the real selector (in-progress ahead of pending, blocked
  skipped) and the `blockTask` mock actually flips the status. This is what makes the
  tests prove the loop *moves on* rather than just asserting a mock was called.
- `makeSummaryDeps(tasks, logs, overrides)` — completion flag present + a fixed task list
  + log capture.

Tests: single revert does not block; **two consecutive reverts block task 1, and the loop
then picks up and finishes task 2** (asserts `spawnClaude` called exactly 3× — two burned
on the stuck task, one on the next — plus the note contains the failing command and the
`tasksFilePath`/`dataDir` are right); fail→pass→fail never blocks (counter reset); the
block is written to the iteration log; summary reports blocked instead of ALL TASKS
COMPLETE; summary still reports ALL TASKS COMPLETE when nothing is blocked; ntfy is
`warning` / `Cairn - Blocked` when blocked; blocked counted on the no-flag stop path.

TDD confirmed: **5 red before the implementation** (the two "does not block" tests pass
vacuously against the old code — they are threshold regression guards, not proofs).

## Verification

- `bun test test/commands/run.test.ts` → **122 pass, 0 fail** (was 114).
- `bun test` → **821 pass, 0 fail**, 29 files (was 813).
- `bun build --target=bun src/index.ts --outfile /tmp/...` → clean.
- `bunx tsc --noEmit` → the only two project-file errors are **pre-existing** (verified by
  stashing: `run.ts` model union, `post-task-reviewer.ts` Task shape). No new ones.

## Notes for the next agent

- This is layer 3 of the stuck-task fix and works standalone. #69 (broadened
  `isCantRunError`) and #70 (per-command cwd) reduce how often a revert is *spurious*;
  this one bounds the damage when one happens anyway. Keep all three.
- If you add a new terminal `ValidationResult.status`, decide explicitly whether it should
  increment, reset, or no-op the counter — the `else if (status === 'passed')` shape means
  anything new silently no-ops.
- Per round constraints: `cairn.json`'s `healthCheck` was NOT modified and `./install.sh`
  was NOT run. The running loop uses the frozen binary, so this change does not take
  effect until the user unpins and rebuilds after the round.

tasks.title: Rewrite the tests-field description in commands/generate-tasks.md
tasks.description:
`commands/generate-tasks.md:120` currently reads: '- **tests**: array of test commands to verify the task (run from the task's directory)'. Task #68 made that false (validation was pinned to the project root), and task 70 has now replaced it again with per-command resolution. This file is installed into every consuming project by `cairn init`, so the stale line actively mis-instructs planners in other repos.

Read `src/test-validator.ts` AS TASK 70 LEFT IT and describe the real rule — do not restate this description, and do not guess. The shape of the answer: commands run from the task's directory by default, and any command whose path arguments do not resolve there but do resolve from the project root is run from the project root — so either form works, and manifest-driven commands (npm test, bun test, cargo test) correctly pick up the service's own manifest in a multi-service repo. Include task 70's chosen definition of a path-shaped argument, since that is the part a planner needs in order to predict the behavior.

Keep the surrounding bullet-list style and keep the length in proportion to its neighbors. This is a docs-only change — do not touch any file under src/ or test/.

Do NOT modify `cairn.json`'s `healthCheck` value and do NOT run `./install.sh` — both are user-managed for this round (the binary is pinned to a frozen copy outside the repo and the health check is redirected to a throwaway outfile). tasks.title: CLAUDE.md truth-up: health check command and the CREATE-vs-RESOLVE standing rule
tasks.description:
Two corrections, both flagged HAS_GAPS in .cairn/reviews/round-8.md and re-verified as still live. CLAUDE.md is the ONLY file you may edit — src/brand.ts, src/utils.ts and src/config.ts are listed for READING so your descriptions match the code.

(a) THE DOCUMENTED HEALTH CHECK DOES NOT EXIST. Three places claim `--target=bun`: the Conventions bullet at ~CLAUDE.md:68 ('The health check must pass --target=bun...'), the pin/unpin intro at ~:91, and pin/unpin step 2 at ~:96. The real build is `bun run build` -> `bun build --compile src/index.ts --outfile dist/cairn` (see package.json). Round 9 explicitly REJECTED the --target=bun form: it emits a plain bundle rather than a standalone executable, so a compile-step failure would pass the check and only surface after unpinning. Replace all three, and rewrite the :68 bullet's RATIONALE — the old text explains why --target=bun is needed, which no longer applies. Explain instead why --compile is the required form: it exercises the same compile step that produces the shipped binary.

CRITICAL: right now cairn.json's healthCheck is TEMPORARILY pinned to `bun build --compile src/index.ts --outfile /tmp/cairn-healthcheck`, an uncommitted round-only redirect. Document the REAL value (`bun run build`, outfile dist/cairn), NOT what you find in cairn.json. Do not treat cairn.json as the source of truth for this, and do not edit cairn.json under any circumstance. Round 9 hit exactly this failure: the pinned value was swept into task #56's commit and became permanent git history.

(b) RESTORE THE CREATE-vs-RESOLVE STANDING RULE. Task #65 deleted the findDataDir/findConfigFile descriptions wholesale instead of rewriting them, but both functions are live (src/utils.ts:36, src/config.ts:12) and src/brand.ts's own doc comment (~lines 6-12) still tells readers the rule lives in CLAUDE.md — where it no longer appears. Restore it to Conventions, phrased against the CURRENT code: BRAND.dataDir / BRAND.configFile / BRAND.socket / BRAND.pidFile are for CREATING paths, never for RESOLVING them; anything pointing at something expected to already exist must come from findDataDir(), findConfigFile(), findNarrationSocketPath(), or findNarrationPidFile(). Keep it to the tightened post-#65 length — this is a restoration, not a re-expansion.

While you are in the pin/unpin section: it stays in CLAUDE.md long-term (the user's call). It is generic guidance for any self-modifying round, not tied to the Ralph->Cairn rename. Add a one-line note saying so, so the question stops being re-litigated each round.

tasks.description:

Rewrite to describe why skipUnchanged/log exist for the three installers as they are used TODAY. Keep the interface and both fields; check the current callers before rewording so the new comment is actually accurate.
(3) The GITIGNORE_CONTENT comment at ~line 38 points at a CLAUDE.md section that no longer exists — "(see CLAUDE.md, 'The temp-file prefix — a second naming tier')", deleted by task #65. Drop the dangling pointer but KEEP the substantive point it introduces: the NOTES_TEMP_PREFIX-spelled scratch line is a permanent exception, not a compatibility leftover, and removing it would let each iteration's scratch file get swept into the agent's own commit.

Then make TEMP_IGNORE_SUFFIXES (~:15), GITIGNORE_CURRENT_HEADER (~:25) and ignoreBlock (~:29) MODULE-PRIVATE by dropping the `export` keyword. tasks.title: Repair the self-contradictory allowlist comment in post-task-reviewer.ts
tasks.description:
`src/post-task-reviewer.ts:142-146` reads: 'The rule is derived from reviewsDir — the same path the prompt tells the reviewer to write — so the two can never diverge. Hardcoding a directory name here would grant an allowlist for e.g. .cairn/reviews/** on a project that actually lives in .cairn/, and every reviewer write would be silently denied with no error and no review output.'

Task #57 applied a literal rename instruction that collapsed BOTH sides of the example to '.cairn', so the illustration now describes a MATCH, not a mismatch — hardcoding .cairn/reviews/** for a project that actually lives in .cairn/ would work fine and would NOT cause a silent denial. The sentence no longer supports its own conclusion. The invariant it guards is load-bearing and is also stated in CLAUDE.md's Agent workflow section.

Rewrite the comment so the illustration actually demonstrates silent denial: contrast a hardcoded BRAND.dataDir-derived glob against a project whose data dir was RESOLVED somewhere else (a nested project, or a CAIRN_PROJECT_ROOT override), so the granted glob and the path in the prompt name genuinely different directories and every Edit/Write is denied with no error and no review output.

Keep the surrounding context intact: the neighboring comment at ~:136-140 about absolute paths and the shell's cwd at evaluation time is correct and separate, and the absDataDir note at ~:125-127 is correct.

THIS IS A COMMENT-ONLY CHANGE. The mechanism — reviewFileRule derived from the same reviewsDir that buildPostTaskReviewUserPrompt targets (~:129, :133, :147) — must not change in any way. Verify `bun test test/post-task-reviewer.test.ts` is green before and after. If no test currently asserts that the granted allowlist rule and the prompt's target path derive from the same value, ADD one — that is precisely the invariant this comment exists to protect, and an untested invariant is how #57 broke it.

Do NOT modify `cairn.json`'s `healthCheck` value and do NOT run `./install.sh` — both are user-managed for this round (the binary is pinned to a frozen copy outside the repo and the health check is redirected to a throwaway outfile). tasks.title: Retire the dead PathProbeDeps seam in narration.ts and settle findDataDir
tasks.description:
`src/narration.ts:26-28` exports PathProbeDeps { exists?: (path: string) => boolean }, and both findNarrationSocketPath(projectRoot?, _deps = {}) (:37) and findNarrationPidFile(_deps = {}) (:52) take it as a leading-underscore parameter they NEVER read. findNarrationSocketPath reads the project's .claude/hooks/narrate.sh and otherwise falls back to BRAND.socket; findNarrationPidFile is an unconditional `return BRAND.pidFile`. The seam's own doc comment admits it: 'With a single candidate per path there is nothing left to probe for, so both resolvers currently ignore it.'

Worse, the tests imply a liveness check that is not performed. In test/narration.test.ts, 'returns the current brand socket when it is already live' (~:327) and 'returns the current brand pid file when it exists' (~:382) both pass an `exists` predicate that is discarded — they would pass identically with no predicate at all, so the titles claim coverage that does not exist. Sibling tests have the same problem to a lesser degree.

Decide ONE way and apply it consistently: either DELETE PathProbeDeps and both _deps parameters and rewrite the affected test titles to describe what is actually asserted (this is the recommended default — the seam has no caller and no second candidate left to probe), or RESTORE real existence checks so the titles become true. Do not leave a third state where the parameter survives unread.

Settle the same question for `src/utils.ts:36` findDataDir, which is likewise an unconditional join(projectRoot, BRAND.dataDir) despite a doc comment about resolving 'data that is expected to already exist'. If you keep it as-is, correct the comment to say it COMPOSES a path rather than probing for one.

CRITICAL — RunRunDeps.findNarrationSocketPath is a DIFFERENT seam and MUST SURVIVE. It is the injection point that lets test/commands/run.test.ts:1434 ('binds the narration server to the resolved socket, not a hardcoded one') mock socket resolution at the run-loop boundary; round 9 deliberately kept it. Confirm that test still passes. Also do NOT remove the projectRoot parameter of findNarrationSocketPath — it is load-bearing hook resolution. Leave StartNarrationDeps (checkHealth/sleep, ~:56-59) alone; it is live and used throughout the tests.

TDD: adjust the test titles and assertions FIRST so they fail against the current code, then make the source match.

Do NOT modify `cairn.json`'s `healthCheck` value and do NOT run `./install.sh` — both are user-managed for this round (the binary is pinned to a frozen copy outside the repo and the health check is redirected to a throwaway outfile).
